basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis Adae et Sellae: Audite vocem meam uxores Lamech, auscultate'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis Adae et Sellae: Audite vocem meam uxores Lamech, auscultate sermonem meum, quoniam occidi virum in vulnus meum, et adolescentulum in livorem meum. Virum vel adolescentulum, quem dicit, Cain significat, quem idem Lamech, sed non sponte, interficit, sicut Hieronymus in quodam Hebraeo volumine scriptum esse testatur. Occidit autem eum in vulnus et in livorem suum, quia et ipse sibi in hoc mortem adscivit ac damnationem, quod eum, quem Deus vitae donaverat, peremit.
